baslik: A Worker Set a Submarine on Fire to Leave Work Early
sonuc: was destroyed by fire during an overhaul
tetik: a shipyard worker lighting rags in a berthing compartment
mekanizma: arson in a submarine under overhaul, spreading through crew, command and torpedo spaces
ders: the submarine was decommissioned instead of repaired
yanilgi: The first explanation blamed a vacuum cleaner. A worker later confessed to starting it.
tartisma: Repairs would have cost hundreds of millions. What's the true price of one person's decision?
basliklar: How a Worker Destroyed USS Miami
The Fire Set to Get Off Work Early
hook: He wanted to go home early
soru: What's the price of one decision?
sahneler: Fire broke out inside the nuclear submarine Miami at a shipyard in Maine.
It spread through crew, command and torpedo spaces, and burned for twelve hours.
The submarine was in overhaul.
The first report blamed a vacuum cleaner.
Then a shipyard worker confessed.
He lit rags on a bunk so he could leave work early.
He was sentenced to more than seventeen years.
The submarine was decommissioned instead of repaired.

baslik: A Brand-New Cruiser Ran Aground Off Honolulu Airport
sonuc: ran aground on a reef off Honolulu
tetik: a grounding near the airport's reef runway at night
mekanizma: a navigation failure putting the cruiser on a coral reef
ders: the captain was relieved and the damaged ship was later slated for early retirement
yanilgi: The damage wasn't only to the ship. Dragging it off also tore up the reef.
tartisma: The Navy later lost confidence the ship was seaworthy. When is a ship never quite the same?
basliklar: Why USS Port Royal Ran Aground
hook: It ran aground by the airport
soru: Is a damaged ship ever the same?
sahneler: At night, the guided missile cruiser Port Royal ran aground off Honolulu.
Suddenly it was stuck on a coral reef near the airport's runway.
It took days to pull it free.
Its sonar dome, propellers and shafts were heavily damaged.
The reef was badly damaged too.
The captain was relieved of duty.
Several officers were disciplined.
The ship was later slated for early retirement.

baslik: Only Two of Three Gates Opened and the Dam Failed
tetik: heavy rain with a spillway gate not fully open
mekanizma: overtopping of an earthen embankment when spillway capacity fell short
ders: the dam was rebuilt and the lake restored in 2016
yanilgi: The rain was extreme, but the dam didn't use all of its spillway.
tartisma: Earlier floods had already damaged the dam. Who should pay for fixing a private dam?
basliklar: The Spillway Gate That Wasn't Open
soru: Who pays for a private dam?
sahneler: After torrential rain, an earthen dam in Iowa failed.
Suddenly the lake behind it drained through the breach.
About ten inches of rain fell in twelve hours.
The river upstream reached record levels.
Only two of the three spillway gates were fully open.
Water overtopped the embankment.
The southern side gave way.
The dam was rebuilt years later.

baslik: The Flood That Created America's Modern Flood Control
tetik: heavy rain and snow on saturated ground
mekanizma: levees failing as the Great Miami River rose
ders: the Miami Conservancy District built dry dams to protect the valley
yanilgi: Dayton flooded often before 1913. Nobody had built a lasting solution.
tartisma: Dry dams now hold floods back only when needed. Why did it take a disaster to build them?
basliklar: The Flood That Changed Flood Control
sahneler: The Great Miami River broke through the levees of Dayton, Ohio.
Suddenly downtown was underwater, in places twenty feet deep.
Heavy rain and snow had saturated the ground.
The area had flooded every few decades.
The existing levees failed.
Ohio passed a law allowing conservancy districts.
The Miami Conservancy District was formed.
It became one of America's first major flood control districts.

baslik: The Man Accused of Breaking a Levee to Strand His Wife
tetik: months of heavy rain on the Mississippi and Missouri basins
mekanizma: prolonged high water overtopping and destroying hundreds of levees
ders: the flood reshaped buyouts and floodplain policy
yanilgi: Not every breach was natural. One man was accused of removing sandbags on purpose.
tartisma: Nearly all private farm levees failed. Should people rebuild in a floodplain?
sahneler: Floodwater broke through levees across the American Midwest.
For months, towns and farms went underwater, and fifty people died.
Months of rain filled the Mississippi and Missouri.
Rivers stayed at record levels for weeks.
Nearly all private farm levees on the Missouri were overtopped or destroyed.
One man was accused of removing sandbags from a levee on purpose.
The breach flooded thousands of acres.
It reshaped how America handles floodplains.

baslik: The Storm Surge That Flooded New York's Subway
sonuc: flooded New York's tunnels and subway
tetik: a record storm surge at high tide
mekanizma: surge water pouring into low-lying tunnels, subway lines and power infrastructure
ders: New York began major resilience projects for tunnels and power
yanilgi: The wind wasn't the main problem in New York. The water was.
tartisma: Rising seas made the surge worse. How do old cities defend their tunnels?
basliklar: How Hurricane Sandy Flooded New York
The Surge That Filled the Subway
soru: How do old cities defend tunnels?
sahneler: Hurricane Sandy's storm surge hit New York City.
Suddenly seawater flooded streets, tunnels and subway lines.
The surge reached about thirteen feet.
Road tunnels had to be closed.
Power was cut across the city.
Sea level had risen over the past century.
That made the surge reach further.
New York began major resilience projects.

baslik: The Worst Blackout in US History
sonuc: knocked out Puerto Rico's power grid for months
tetik: a catastrophic hurricane hitting a weakened grid
mekanizma: a fragile, underfunded grid destroyed and slow to restore
ders: Puerto Rico's grid became a case study in infrastructure resilience
yanilgi: Most deaths didn't come in the storm itself. Many came in the long months after.
tartisma: The utility had lost 30 percent of its workforce. Is resilience built before the storm?
basliklar: Why Puerto Rico Lost Power for Months
hook: The lights stayed off for months
soru: Is resilience built before the storm?
sahneler: Hurricane Maria tore across Puerto Rico.
Suddenly the island's entire power grid went dark.
It became the worst blackout in US history.
It lasted for months.
The utility was already deep in debt.
It had lost a large part of its workforce.
An estimated two thousand nine hundred seventy five people died in Puerto Rico.
The grid became a case study in resilience.

baslik: Why So Many Schools Collapsed in the Sichuan Earthquake
tetik: a massive earthquake striking during school hours
mekanizma: shoddy construction causing school buildings to collapse
ders: the collapses fuelled demands for accountability in construction
yanilgi: Many nearby buildings stood. Schools fell because of how they were built.
tartisma: Parents demanded answers. Who is accountable when schools fail?
sahneler: A massive earthquake struck Sichuan, China, during school hours.
Suddenly school buildings collapsed, burying students inside.
In one city, a whole school fell with nine hundred students.
Fewer than sixty survived.
Eight schools toppled in that city alone.
Thousands of schoolchildren died.
Shoddy construction was blamed.
Parents demanded accountability.

baslik: The Earthquake That Exposed Soviet Construction
mekanizma: poorly built apartment blocks collapsing without survival space
ders: the disaster exposed substandard Soviet building practices
yanilgi: Well-built buildings survived. Poorly built ones collapsed completely.
tartisma: Hospitals collapsed and doctors died. How do you plan for the rescuers being victims?
basliklar: Why the 1988 Armenian Earthquake Was So Deadly
The Buildings That Collapsed in Spitak
sahneler: A strong earthquake struck northern Armenia near Spitak.
Within seconds, apartment blocks collapsed, killing at least twenty five thousand people.
Spitak, Leninakan and Kirovakan were devastated.
Many buildings pancaked without survival space.
Well-built buildings survived.
Hospitals collapsed and many doctors died.
Soviet media began discussing substandard construction.
It exposed how buildings had been built.

baslik: The Wingless Aircraft That Crashed on Landing
sonuc: tumbled across the lake bed on landing
tetik: a pilot-induced oscillation and a distraction
mekanizma: a hard-to-control wingless body, a distraction, and poor height cues on an unmarked surface
ders: the craft was rebuilt with a centre fin for stability
yanilgi: The pilot survived the crash but lost vision in one eye from an infection.
tartisma: The crash footage became famous on television. Does fame change what we learn from failure?
sahneler: A wingless NASA test aircraft slammed into a dry lake bed on landing.
Suddenly it tumbled over and over across the desert floor.
It was a lifting body, using its shape to fly.
Near the ground, it began rolling side to side.
The pilot regained control.
Then a helicopter seemed to threaten a collision.
He drifted to an unmarked area where height was hard to judge.
The craft was rebuilt with a centre fin.

baslik: The Ranger Who Held His Crew Inside a Mine
sonuc: burned over three million acres in the Northwest
tetik: many fires merging in hurricane-force winds
mekanizma: hundreds of fires joining into a massive blaze driven by wind
ders: the fire shaped the Forest Service's fire suppression policy
yanilgi: Most of the dead weren't residents. They were firefighters.
tartisma: The fire led to aggressive suppression for decades. Did stopping every fire create bigger ones later?
basliklar: The Big Burn and Ranger Pulaski
hook: He held them in a mine
soru: Did stopping fires make them worse?
sahneler: In the American Northwest, many wildfires merged into one massive blaze.
Within two days it burned whole towns, killing eighty seven people.
Most of the dead were firefighters.
Ranger Ed Pulaski led his crew into a mine tunnel.
He held them there as the fire passed.
More than three million acres burned.
It raised public awareness of forest conservation.
It shaped fire suppression policy for decades.

baslik: Lava Opened Fissures Inside a Housing Subdivision
sonuc: destroyed neighbourhoods on Hawaii's Big Island
tetik: fissures opening in the Leilani Estates subdivision
mekanizma: rift-zone eruption through a residential area built on the volcano's flank
ders: the eruption raised questions about building in lava hazard zones
yanilgi: The lava didn't come from a summit far away. It erupted inside the neighbourhood.
tartisma: Homes were built on an active rift zone. Should building there be allowed?
sahneler: Cracks split the roads of a Hawaii subdivision, then lava burst out.
Suddenly lava fountains rose inside Leilani Estates.
Earthquakes and ground deformation came first.
Twenty four fissures opened in and near the neighbourhood.
Lava rivers buried part of a highway.
Another flow destroyed Vacationland Hawaii.
The homes sat on an active rift zone.
It raised questions about building in lava zones.
